page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with no margin notes. Page number top left, running head "HYPOMNEMATA" top right of the text. Catchword "sub" at the bottom right.

main_text.p: ἀμῶς[?] alibi denotare, obscurum non est: tamen, cum præstet simplici & natiuæ sententiæ, cū datur, insistere, fateor me malle sequi eorum sententiam, qui huncversum esse iudicat poeticam, postremi lemmatis versus præcedentis, expositionem. Poeticam voco, quia constat ὑποποιΐας[?] ὡς[?] τῇ ὑπαλλαγῇ[?], velut orationis luminib.sple[?]-didisimis. Ethopœia est, quia in descriptione fontium diuersis in locis erumpe-tium, terramq; rigantium, montes partu-rientes, & voraginem maximo cum sonitu aquas ebullientem, introducit. Hypalage aut est, cum rebus inanimatis, montibus, voraginibus & aquis ea tribuit, quæ sunt animatarum quarundam creaturarum propria.

Primò id quod docet sensus gramma-ticus, Deū videlicet pro suo arbitrio vel cœlitus pluendo, vel fontes excitando, terram irrigare & fœcundam reddere: aut etiam cohibitis pluvijs, aut exiccatis fontibus, ἀντιθέσει[?] sterilitatem inuehere. Iuxta dicta:
Deut.28.23. Erunt què cœli tui, qui sunt supra caput tuum, ærei: & terra, quæ est sub

page.notes: Greek words in the first line and in the Poetica sentence are hard to read and are marked [?]; they are not checked letter by letter. "sple-didisimis" is printed with a long s and a mark over the e; reading uncertain. "huncuer sum" is split across a line end with no hyphen and is copied whole as huncversum. "obseruabimus" was normalised to observabimus. Deut.28.23 is copied as printed, not checked against the Vulgate. The catchword is shown as "sub" with a printed mark, which is uncertain.
